name: Hypothesis testing

subjectOf.text: Linear, robust, and non-linear regression models all show positive and statistically significant coefficients, and compliance costs per unit of AUM do not diminish in the sample, so the hypothesis that smaller advisers pay relatively more is not supported.
subjectOf.abstract: Figures X and Y show that linear, robust, and non-linear regression models show positive and statistically significant coefficients. Compliance costs per unit AUM do not diminish in the sample. There is thus no support for the hypothesis.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: the 2012 survey sample of registered private fund advisers

subjectOf.text: The authors reject Hypothesis 1: they find no evidence that the market reacts negatively to the N/DPA announcement and the start of the term and positively to the end of the term, contrary to the cost-imposition view of N/DPAs.
subjectOf.abstract: There is no evidence to support Hypothesis 1: The market does not react negatively at ANDPAE (E1a) and BNDPAT (E1b) and positively at ENDPAT (E1c).
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, Stock Price Response to Non- and Deferred Prosecution Agreements (2015). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2629451

subjectOf.text: The data support Hypothesis 2: the market reacts positively at the DOJ announcement and at the start of the N/DPA term and negatively at the end of the term.
